## Triage

**Type: `bug`** — the automation loops on its own comments: six full LLM runs on a single fixture (#678) with no reporter input. The `bug` label on the issue replaced the pre-set `chore`: it is not tooling housekeeping but a defect in the trigger.

**Priority: `priority:high`** — not critical. There is no outage, data loss or security problem, and the repo has no code to change. But it burns budget on every automated comment and floods issues, and it must be fixed before any `needs-info` re-check runs again, so it should not sit.

**Status: `ready`** — implementable without questions: the trigger condition, the root cause (own comments satisfy `issue_comment.created` while `needs-info` is present, and the bot posts as `adminypc` so `sender.login` cannot separate it), and three concrete fixes are all given. Not a `question` (it asks for a change), and no duplicate exists (#678 is the fixture, #679 the companion label-sync PR).

### Evidence used
- Issue #680 body. Comment IDs 6033463611, 6033544703, 6033583588, 6033607971, 6033685344, 6033692833 on #678 (07:49–08:04 UTC), every one authored by `adminypc`.
- #678 state: `chore`, `priority:low`, `needs-info`; body "Fixture for testing issue-label-sync.sh. Safe to delete."
- Repo search for needs-info re-check / loop / needs-info in titles: 1 result, #680 itself.
- `grep` of `.github/`, `.claude/`, `scripts/`, `docs/` for the re-check: no matches. The trigger is configured in the automation backend, not in this repository, so there is no source change to ship — the fix is a trigger/config change on the automation itself.

### Notes for whoever fixes it
Preferred fix is #1 (post as a distinct bot account) — it is the only one that survives the reporter and the automation sharing the `adminypc` account. Fix #2 (body-marker filter `!icontains(comment.body, 'AI agent (OpenHands)')`) is the smallest change that stops the current loop. Either way the trigger should also stop re-firing on label application; fix #3 is the most conservative.

## Triage

**Severity: high (P1) — active, self-sustaining budget loop; not data loss.**

The loop is not only historical; it is running now. At triage time issue #678 had grown to **8** `Needs-info re-check` comments, the newest at `2026-10-07T08:12:21Z` (id `6033817542`), i.e. within a minute of this run. Because every run is a full LLM conversation and each run's own comment is the next run's trigger, the cost does not stop on its own. That is why it is P1 and not P2: the failure mode is unbounded, not a one-off.

**Labels applied:** `bug` (defect in the automation's trigger, not a feature request), `priority:high`. No duplicate found — searched open and closed issues for `needs-info`, `re-trigger`, `automation loop`; the only other hit is the fixture #678 itself.

### Area / module responsible

The defective trigger is **not** in this repository. `grep -rI "needs-info"` over the whole tree returns nothing, PR #679 (`test/label-sync`) is not merged, and there is no workflow, script, or config that defines the `needs-info` re-check. The automation's trigger (`type: event`, `on: issue_comment.created`, filtered on the `needs-info` label) lives in the **OpenHands automations backend**, not in `apps/` or `.github/`. So there is no path here to change (for example `apps/api/src/modules/...` or `apps/web/src/app/...`) that can fix it, and no PR is open for it.

### Root cause (as filed, confirmed)

1. Trigger = `needs-info` present **and** a new comment.
2. The automation posts its own comment and posts under the **reporter's account** (`adminypc`, `user.type: User`), so `sender.login`/`user.type` cannot tell it apart from the reporter.
3. Its own comment satisfies condition 1, re-arming itself.

### Suggested next step

A maintainer needs to change the automation definition in the **automations backend** (no repo file can). Preferred, in order:

1. **Re-scope the trigger away from `issue_comment.created`.** Fire on `issues.labeled` with `contains(issue.labels[].name, 'needs-info')` — one run when the label is applied — and optionally require a positive trigger phrase in a later reply. This removes the self-trigger structurally rather than trying to detect it.
2. If it must keep watching comments, **exclude its own output by body marker** (`!icontains(comment.body, 'generated by an AI agent (OpenHands)')`). The footer is present on every comment in the loop.
3. **Post as a distinct bot account** so a `sender.type == 'Bot'` guard works.

Until the trigger is fixed, every automation run should also short-circuit when the triggering comment is its own — but that is a mitigation, not the fix.

### Credential gap

I could not apply the backend-side fix: the automations API is not reachable from this sandbox (no automations host/session key is injected; `RUNTIME_URL` is set but no API credential is). This agent only holds the repo's GitHub token. The trigger change needs someone with access to the automations backend, or a credential supplied to this automation.

**Why no PR:** the defect is in an automation definition outside this repository, so there is nothing in-tree to change and nothing to exercise with the repo's gates.

## Effort estimate

**Size: XS — but the fix is not in this repository.** The change is a one-line edit to the *trigger filter* of the `needs-info` re-check automation (OpenHands events backend), not a file under git. There is no checked-in definition of that automation: PR #679 added `.github/scripts/issue-label-sync.sh`, `duplicate-sweep.sh` and `pr-lifecycle.sh` plus their workflows, and a grep for `needs-info` / `issue_comment` / `OpenHands` across `.github/`, `docs/`, `scripts/` and `.claude/` finds no automation config. So a repo PR cannot fix the loop today; the work is (a) a config edit outside the repo, and optionally (b) a short decision/runbook note under `.claude/memory/` or `docs/`.

The loop is **still running** while this is written: #678 now holds at least eight "Needs-info re-check" comments (ids `6033463611` → `6033843173`, 07:49Z → 08:14Z), each one firing the next run.

### The three fixes, sized

| Fix | Size | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Append `&& !icontains(comment.body, 'AI agent (OpenHands)')` to the trigger filter | **XS** | automation `trigger.filter` | Every automated comment ends with the mandated AI-disclosure footer; a human reply never does. No new account, no new secret, one clause. |
| Post the re-check as a **distinct bot account** | **S** | automation identity + `trigger.filter` (`sender.type == 'Bot'`) | Robust — independent of wording — but needs a new GitHub account, a token, and a least-privilege secret allowlist. |
| Narrow the trigger to `issues.labeled` + a positive reply phrase | **S** | automation `trigger.on` / `filter` | Changes behaviour (no re-check on human replies), so it is a redesign, not only a bug fix. |

### Files / areas likely touched

- **Outside the repo:** the `needs-info` re-check automation definition — its `trigger.on` (`issue_comment.created`) and `trigger.filter`. This is the actual fix.
- **If a record is wanted in-repo:** a `.claude/memory/` decision/lesson note, or `docs/` — pinning the exact disclosure marker as the loop guard.
- **No** `.github/scripts/*` or workflow change is required; none exists for this automation.

### Main risks

1. **The marker is exact-match.** The filter must pin the literal disclosure string (`_This comment was created by an AI agent (OpenHands) on behalf of the repository maintainers._`). If that wording changes, the loop silently returns — the marker should be noted wherever it is defined.
2. **Sender identity cannot separate the automation.** Confirmed on #678: every comment, including the re-checks, is `adminypc` with `user.type: User`. `sender.login` / `sender.type` alone cannot break the cycle — only a body marker or a real bot account can.
3. **A bot account forks the secret surface.** Give it an explicit allowlist, never every secret.
4. **No test can guard this from the repo** unless the automation definition is checked in, so golden rule #7 cannot apply to config that lives outside the tree. A regression guard needs the definition in-repo.
5. **CI minutes.** Not triggered by this fix (no repo file), but the repo has already hit an Actions billing wall (`.claude/memory/lessons/github-actions-minutes-exhausted.md`) — relevant only if a workflow is added alongside the fix.

### Calibrated against

- **#679** — *test: label sync* — the companion automation tooling (`issue-label-sync.sh`, `duplicate-sweep.sh`, `pr-lifecycle.sh` + 3 workflows): 7 files, +377. Open, not merged.
- **#534** — *ci: skip every job when a change has no code* — closest **merged** precedent for changing an automation's trigger/scope: 7 files, +281/−27, incl. `change-scope.sh` and a guard test.
- **#664** — *deploy watchdog* (`.github/scripts` + workflow + guard test): 5 files, +622. Open.
- **#677** — *k6 load tests* (scheduled-workflow tooling + runner unit suite): 10 files, +1015. Open.
- **#660** — *chore: add OpenHands setup, hooks, skill bridge* — precedent for repo-side agent tooling. Open.
- **#678** — the fixture where the loop was observed; **#679** is its companion PR.

### Questions that would unblock it

1. Where does the `needs-info` re-check automation live — the OpenHands automations backend only, or should its definition be checked in so a PR can change and test it?
2. Which fix: the body-marker filter (XS, no new account) or a distinct bot account (S, robust)?
3. If a bot account: what is the least-privilege secret allowlist for it?
4. Should the re-check back off after N automated passes with no human reply?
5. Should the chosen marker be recorded as a decision/lesson so the guard is reviewable?

**Loop stopped at its source (evidence for this issue).**

A terminal pass on #678 removed its `needs-info` label and applied `invalid` (the fixture's own body — *"Fixture for testing issue-label-sync.sh. Safe to delete."* — declares it disposable, and it is not waiting on reporter detail). Since the re-check trigger requires `needs-info` to be present, comment id `6033866832` (08:18Z) is the last `Needs-info re-check` comment on #678 — the self-triggering cycle described here no longer has a live issue to feed on.

This does **not** fix the defect: the trigger will re-arm itself on the next genuinely `needs-info` issue whose reporter replies, and any *automated* comment on such an issue will still re-trigger a run. The fix recommended in the body still stands, and it is not in this repository — there is no checked-in definition of the `needs-info` re-check automation to edit (confirmed by grep across `.github/`, `scripts/`, `docs/`, `.claude/`; #679 only adds the unrelated `issue-label-sync.sh` tooling).

## Root cause found

The `needs-info` re-check fires on `issue_comment.created` while the issue carries `needs-info`. After it posts its comment, a comment exists *and* the label is still present — so it satisfies its own trigger and re-arms. On #678 that produced 6 back-to-back “Needs-info re-check” comments in ~15 minutes, each a full LLM conversation.

`sender.login` / `sender.type` cannot separate it: the comments were posted as `adminypc` (`type: User`), the same account as the reporter, so a `sender.login != …` or `sender.type == 'Bot'` guard would not have matched on its own.

## The trigger is not in this repository

A repo-wide grep (`.github/`, `docs/`, `scripts/`, `.claude/`) for `needs-info`, `issue_comment.created`, `icontains` and JMESPath finds **no** trigger definition, and `git log -S needs-info` shows no commit ever added one. This is an **OpenHands event automation** — the fix is a filter edit in the automation backend, not a code change in the monorepo. A repo PR can record the rule but cannot apply it.

Three filters that break the loop:

1. Post as a distinct bot account, then exclude it: `sender.login != 'cipansor-bot'`.
2. Exclude by the AI footer every automated comment carries: `!icontains(comment.body, 'generated by an AI agent')`.
3. Fire on `issues.labeled` with `contains(issue.labels[].name, 'needs-info')` instead of every comment — the label is applied once, so nothing posted afterwards can re-fire it.

Until the backend filter changes, removing the `needs-info` label stops an in-flight loop — a mitigation, not the fix.

## What I did

- Opened draft PR #681 adding `.claude/memory/lessons/automation-self-trigger-loop.md` (+ INDEX entry) with the root cause, the three exclusions and how to verify a backend change.
- Could **not** apply the backend fix: the automation API answered `401 Invalid or expired API key`, and no `OPENHANDS_API_KEY` / `AGENT_SERVER_URL` / `SANDBOX_ID` was present in the run.

## What is needed to close this

Access to the automation backend: `GET /api/automation/v1/{id}` to read the current trigger, apply one of the three exclusions, then re-test with `POST …/{id}/dispatch` on a throwaway issue before re-enabling. If you can provide a working automation API token, I can complete and verify the trigger change directly.

### Reproduced ✅ (live, against the current repository)

`GET /repos/ypcipansor/cipansor/issues/678/comments`, pulled at 08:17 UTC, returns **11** `Needs-info re-check` comments — every one posted by `adminypc` (`user.type: User`), none from any other account:

(The issue body's table lists 6; by the time of this run it was 11. The cadence — a new comment roughly every 1–4 minutes, each close behind the previous — is the signature of a run triggered by the previous run's own comment.)

Exact command:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://api.github.com/repos/ypcipansor/cipansor/issues/678/comments?per_page=100"
```

### Root cause — confirmed as reported

The trigger is `issue_comment.created` **plus** "issue carries `needs-info`". The automation's own comment is itself an `issue_comment.created` event on an issue that still carries `needs-info`, so each run re-arms the next. The automation posts under `adminypc` — the same account as the reporter — so `sender.login` / `user.type` cannot separate it from a human reply. The loop only stopped because #678's `needs-info` label was removed (final state: `invalid`, `chore`, `priority:low`).

### Why this run opens no PR

**The trigger is not in this repository.** `git grep` across `main` and all 21 remote heads finds no automation definition — no needs-info/re-check filter, no `issue_comment.created` trigger. The repo's `.github/workflows/` (and the label-sync branch `test/label-sync`) hold only CI, deploy, e2e, label-sync and the deploy watchdog; those post as `github-actions[bot]`, whereas these comments are authored by a `User`, i.e. an OpenHands automation running under `adminypc`. The trigger and filter are configured on the OpenHands automation platform, which this run cannot reach: the sandbox session key is scoped to its own conversation and returns `HTTP 401 {"detail":"Invalid or expired API key"}` against `GET /api/automation/v1`. There is no code in the tree for a failing test to target, so a PR here could not change the behaviour.

### Recommended fix (platform-side; the current state already stops the bleeding)

Pick one, in order of robustness:

1. **Exclude the automation's own comments by footer.** Every loop comment ends with `_This comment was generated by an AI agent (OpenHands) ..._`. Add to the trigger filter:

   ```
   !icontains(comment.body, 'AI agent (OpenHands)')
   ```

   One-line change to the existing automation; no identity change needed.

2. **Post as a distinct bot identity** (a GitHub App / bot account) and exclude via `sender.type == 'Bot'` — cleanest long term, but needs an account change.

3. **Narrow the trigger** to `issues.labeled` + `contains(issue.labels[].name, 'needs-info')`, so it fires when the label is applied rather than on every subsequent comment.

Whichever is chosen, a guard worth adding: re-check only on a **positive trigger phrase** or a **different author**, so a `needs-info` issue cannot consume a run per automated comment.

### What is needed from a maintainer

Access to the automation platform — or a maintainer's decision on which option above to take — to edit the `needs-info re-check` trigger. This run has no credential that reaches it, so it reports rather than guessing at a change.

## Investigation — where the loop lives, and what the fix must touch

I traced the `needs-info` re-check trigger to confirm your root-cause analysis and to determine whether it can be fixed in this repository. Summary: **the defect is real, correctly diagnosed, and it is not fixable by a code change in this repo** — the trigger lives in the external OpenHands automation service. Below is the evidence and the exact configuration change to apply there.

### Verified: no automation definition exists in the repository

Searched the checked-out tree plus every remote branch (23 branches) and all of `main`, `.github/`, `.claude/skills`, `.claude/hooks`, `.claude/memory`, `docs/`, `.openhands/`:

```
git grep -l -iE "needs-info|re-check|issue_comment|icontains|automation/v1|preset/prompt" <HEAD>   # no automation definition
bot scrape of all 23 branches for .github/** containing needs|recheck|triage|automation|comment|sweep|lifecycle|stale
  -> only test/label-sync: .github/{scripts,workflows}/{issue-label-sync,pr-lifecycle,duplicate-sweep}.*
```

`.github/scripts/issue-label-sync.sh` (PR #679) only mirrors **type + priority** labels between a PR and the issue it closes; it does **not** copy lifecycle labels (`needs-info`, `question`, `ready`, …) and contains no `issue_comment` trigger. The `needs-info` re-check is an OpenHands automation registered against this repo — definitions live in the automation service, not on disk here.

### Confirmed: the loop is the automation re-triggering on its own output

Your evidence matches the automation-service event model exactly: an automation with `trigger.on = "issue_comment.created"` and a `filter` that is satisfied by `needs-info` present. The automation posts a comment as `adminypc`; that comment is itself an `issue_comment.created` event on a `needs-info` issue, so it satisfies its own condition. Because it posts under the reporter's account (`user.type: "User"`), `sender.type == 'Bot'` and `sender.login` cannot separate it — as you found.

### Why I did not open a PR

Fixing this requires editing the automation definition in the OpenHands automation service (`PATCH /api/automation/v1/{id}` / re-creating it via `/api/automation/v1/preset/prompt`). I do **not** have a credential that can read or patch that definition:

- `AUTOMATION_SESSION_URL` + `SESSION_API_KEY` → `401 {"detail":"Invalid or expired API key"}`
- `https://app.all-hands.dev/api/automation/v1` with the same key → `401`
- The agent-server settings API exposes no automation endpoint (`/api/automation/v1` → `404 Not Found`)

Per the operating rules I stop here rather than guess at a result. **What is missing: an automation-service admin API key** (or an `AGENT_SERVER_URL` + session key scoped to the owning org) able to list and `PATCH` the `needs-info` re-check automation.

### Exact fix to apply in the automation service (recommended: option 2, no repo change, no new bot account)

Keep `trigger.on = "issue_comment.created"` and extend the JMESPath `filter` so the automation's own comments cannot wake it. The AI-disclosure footer your comments already carry is a stable discriminator:

```
contains(issue.labels[].name, 'needs-info') &&
!icontains(comment.body, 'AI agent (OpenHands)') &&
!icontains(comment.body, 'Needs-info re-check')
```

Defense in depth — also drop any event where the commenter is a bot, and only act on the reporter's input:

```
contains(issue.labels[].name, 'needs-info') &&
!icontains(comment.body, 'AI agent (OpenHands)') &&
!(sender.type == 'Bot')
```

Trade-offs of the three options you listed:

1. **Distinct bot account** — most robust (`sender.type == 'Bot'` becomes a clean discriminator), but it is the largest change (new account, token, wiring) and is not required to stop the loop.
2. **Body-marker exclusion (above)** — smallest change, works today, and needs no new account. Recommended first step.
3. **Narrow to `issues.labeled`** — stops the churn but also stops the automation from noticing the reporter's clarifying reply, which is the whole point of a `needs-info` re-check; I would not take this one without a replacement trigger for reporter comments.

### Fixture cleanup (#678)

#678 is a fixture whose body already says *"Safe to delete."* and it is now tagged `invalid`. Recommend closing it as `not_planned` once the filter above is in place, so the fix is verified on a fresh throwaway issue rather than re-triggering on the existing one. (I did not delete or close it — that is a maintainer call, and closing an issue is not something I do unprompted.)

### Verification plan once the credential is available

1. Create a throwaway issue, comment as a non-reporter, apply `needs-info`.
2. Post one automation comment; confirm the next `issue_comment.created` event is filtered out (no run).
3. Confirm a genuine reporter reply **does** start one run.
4. Close the throwaway.

If you can supply an automation-service API key, I can apply the filter change and run that verification end to end.
